newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Kuwait Bank to double capital.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Kuwait Bank to double capital.

text.p: Jordan Kuwait Bank said on Monday it would double its capital to 20 million dinars by moving 4.5 million dinars from reserves and retained profits and raising another 5.5 million through share subscription.

Bank Chairman Sufian al-Sartawi told Reuters the proposals, meeting Central Bank requirements to increase capital to 20 million dinars by the end of the year, would be put to shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting next month.
He said the new shares would be offered to existing shareholders but there might be a public offering too.
"It will be according to the decision of the shareholders' meeting," Sartawi said.
He said the bank reported net profits of three million dinars in 1996 and was aiming to expand its banking activities in the Gulf.
Brokers said on Sunday Gulf investors bought 500,000 shares in the bank, or five percent of its share equity, raising the stake of Gulf shareholders in the bank close to 50 percent.
"It's good for the bank. We have investors with good capital and that can help us in the Gulf," Sartawi said.
He said the plans for capital increase and the latest share purchases would put an end to talk of a merger between Jordan Kuwait Bank and Bank of Jordan.
"You cannot make a merger without approval from 75 percent of the shareholders," Sartawi said. "There was never that level of support for the merger."

Bankers said last month the boards of the two banks had revived plans for a merger which go back three years when they agreed the idea on principle. The idea was encouraged by the Central Bank, which has pushed for mergers to help create a leaner and stronger banking system. -- Amman Newsroom + 9626-623776
